newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen down on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen down on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares fell after Wednesday's slight gain and analysts said the stronger selling after price fixing suggested the current downward correction after the recent bank-led surge should continue on Monday.
The bourse is closed on Friday for the Assumption holiday.
But analysts said the market, which gained 14.5 percent over six-sessions earlier this month, could soon rebound.

"Firms in the construction, power and furniture industries which are gaining from the recent flooding are a lot cheaper than comparable firms in Hungary or Russia," said Dariusz Piszczatowksi of Polish Development Bank (PBR) house.

The main market's all-share index fell 1.7 percent to 16,920.4 points and turnover fell 37.6 percent to 167.9 million zlotys ($48.2 million) on all three markets. Losers led gainers by 94 to nine with 10 stocks flat.
Biggest loser bank PBR hit a correction after its recent surge, falling 10 percent in light trade with stronger buying after price fixing.
Analysts said electrode maker ZEW, down 9.8 percent and extending its downtrend on flood damage, could finally be approaching a bottom.
They were surprised by the scale of builder Mostostal Warszawa's 9.8-percent jump.
